data.title: 51Talk Student from Indonesia Takes the Stage at COP31 to Speak on Climate Change
data.description:
Athar shares his perspective on climate change at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, joining young participants from six countries on the global stage.

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Athar, a young student from Indonesia, took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share his thoughts on climate change and the future of the planet.

Speaking alongside young participants from Türkiye, China, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Thailand, Athar delivered his message in English, addressing the climate concerns, questions, and hopes of Indonesian children for a better environmental future. His participation demonstrated how children can use English to communicate their ideas and contribute to conversations that extend beyond their own communities.

Athar was among nine young participants from six countries supported by 51Talk, a global 1-on-1 online English education platform.

Since 2019, 51Talk has helped young learners share their perspectives at UN events, with COP31 marking the fifth time the company has brought young participants to speak on a UN stage.

Athar's Experience on the Global Stage

For Athar, 9, from Jakarta, participating in COP31 was an opportunity to speak about an issue that matters to him while experiencing what it means to address an international audience.

In his presentation, Athar shared his perspective on environmental responsibility, highlighting how small actions, such as reducing plastic waste and taking care of nature, can make a difference in protecting our planet. He encouraged listeners to take collective action for a healthier and more sustainable future for the next generation.

"I was a little nervous at first, but when I stood on the stage, I felt happy and proud. It was a great opportunity for me to share my thoughts and bring the perspectives of Indonesian children to the world," Athar said.

Ahead of the conference, Athar prepared for his speech through 51Talk's 1-on-1 online English lessons and dedicated speech practice, with support from his family. Working with his English teachers, he practiced organizing his thoughts and expressing his ideas clearly and confidently in English.

The experience also offered opportunities beyond public speaking. During his time in Antalya, Athar met young participants from different countries, exchanged ideas, and experienced firsthand how a shared language can bring people together.

"It was a special experience for me to meet people from different countries and share my thoughts about protecting our planet. I hope the questions I brought from Indonesian children can help more people listen to what children think about our future," Athar added.

Building Speaking Confidence Beyond the Classroom

At 51Talk, learning English is about more than developing language proficiency. It is also about helping children gain the confidence to express themselves and communicate in real-world situations.

51Talk combines personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers supported by professional training and teaching standards. Through interactive lessons and individualized guidance, children have regular opportunities to practice speaking, share opinions, and strengthen their communication skills.

Athar's participation at COP31 reflects this approach, showing how English learning can create opportunities for children to share their ideas on an international stage.

"Seeing Athar take part in COP31 is a proud moment for us. From his experience at the Global Youth Summit to this international climate conference, he continues to show that children can make meaningful contributions to important global conversations. We are glad to support his journey and see him take this opportunity to represent Indonesia," said Martin, General Manager of 51Talk Indonesia.

To further support practical communication skills, 51Talk introduced Global Communicator in 2026, a curriculum designed to connect English learning with real-world communication. Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, Global Communicator features immersive, task-based activities built around everyday situations and cross-cultural topics. AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help address individual learning needs and make progress more visible to families.

About 51Talk

Founded in 2011, 51Talk is a global 1-on-1 online English education platform for children aged 3 to 15. Through interactive lessons, structured curricula, and personalized instruction, 51Talk helps young learners build practical English communication skills and speaking confidence.

For more information, visit: https://www.51talk.com/id/index/

SOURCE 51Talk

data.title: Half of wallets on Trump’s dinner list got tokens from non-US exchanges
data.description:
More than half the wallets that qualified for Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner on Sunday received TRUMP tokens from crypto exchanges that bar US users, according to analysis from consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

Trump is hosting his second dinner for his top memecoin holders at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, more than a year after an inaugural dinner in May 2025. The dinner offers up to 185 seats based on time-weighted TRUMP holdings.

Public Citizen said it traced 66 of the 130 wallets on the public leaderboard to exchanges including Binance (the global exchange), Bybit and BloFin — which are not permitted to serve US citizens. The list also included 15 of the 29 wallets that qualified for a VIP reception with the president.

“If those bans are enforced, many of the people vying for a seat at the president’s table don’t live in the United States,” said Public Citizen research director Zach Everson.

Trump’s memecoin events have drawn scrutiny over whether foreign buyers can essentially buy access to the president. Democratic lawmakers called on the White House to release the guest list for the first dinner in May 2025, while some joined a protest outside the golf club. They renewed the request again in October.

Who qualified for Trump’s memecoin dinner?

FastX, a Singapore-linked crypto trading platform, was the top-ranked wallet, holding $1.65 million in TRUMP at the time of the snapshot on Nov. 16.

The third highest ranked wallet has been linked to Unitas, a stablecoin issuer run by a British Virgin Islands company, according to Public Citizen.

Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands and founder and CEO of AirdropAlert, shared a picture from the Trump gala dinner on X. He came 26th with $45,351 in time-weighted TRUMP holdings.

Public Citizen also identified 14 wallets it suspects were controlled by the same person or group. Each received approximately 3,700 TRUMP tokens from Binance in October before being emptied weeks ahead of the cutoff.

Tron founder Justin Sun, the top-ranked holder at the May 2025 dinner, was expected to skip the event, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Meanwhile, Trump is a featured speaker for the event, and guests also include Floyd Mayweather, “Shark Tank” investor Kevin O’Leary, former NBA player Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Suchard.

Trump token down 99% from peak

The gala dinner comes even as the TRUMP token trades 98.8% below its all-time high of $75.35.

Trump held the first dinner for TRUMP holders in May 2025 at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, when the token was trading at $14.43. By the time he held his second memecoin event, a conference and luncheon at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, the token had already dropped to $2.88.

As of the time of writing, the TRUMP token is trading at $0.89.

data.title: Libya's NOC says 'unlawful' pipeline closure from Sharara oilfield to cut output by 350,000 bpd
data.description:
Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said on Monday the closure of a valve on a pipeline from the Sharara oilfield, one of Libya's largest, by an "unlawful group" would result in the loss of around 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) of production.

A second pipeline, linking the Hamada field to the country's largest refinery, Zawiya, has also remained closed for more than two weeks, resulting in the loss of around 15,000 bpd, the NOC said, bringing Libya's total oil production losses to approximately 365,000 bpd.

The NOC said in October that an armed group had shut a valve on the main Hamada crude oil pipeline, halting flows. The Corporation said on Saturday that the forced closure of the Hamada oil pipeline had cost the country more than $30.8 million, renewing its condemnation of attacks on oil facilities.

Located ​in southwestern Libya, Sharara ​is operated ⁠by a joint venture of the state-owned NOC via Acacus oil company with Spain's Repsol , France's TotalEnergies , Austria's ​OMV and Norway's Equinor .

Libyan oil output has been subject to repeated closures for political ​and technical reasons since the 2011 uprising against Muammar Gaddafi.

Oil production is Libya's main economic resource, representing ​approximately 90% ⁠of its economy.

data.title: Axel REE Appoints WSP Australia to Conduct Woolrich ISR Field Program
data.description:
Axel REE has appointed global engineering consultancy WSP Australia to lead the technical studies, planning, design, and execution of the Woolrich deposit in situ recovery (ISR) field program within its Caladão rare earth-gallium project in Brazil.

WSP’s expertise will support the integration of hydrogeological and potential geotechnical investigations into the design and implementation of the program, which will evaluate the behaviour of magnesium sulphate ISR under certain field conditions.

These will include solution migration through the mineralised regolith, hydraulic containment, and the recovery of rare earth-bearing pregnant leach solution (PLS).

Axel is now advancing the remaining technical and operational activities required for field program execution, including completion of auger drilling, integration of leach results from SGS Laboratories, and advancing WSP’s specialist investigations.

Priority ISR Deposit

Woolrich, which is Axel’s priority deposit for the development and field validation of its proposed magnesium sulphate ISR process, hosts a mineral resource of 264.6 million tonnes at 1,101 parts per million total rare earth oxides (TREO) including a maiden 110.1Mt indicated resource at 1,073ppm TREO.

It is one of four defined rare earth deposits within the Caladão project, which hosts a global resource of 708.6Mt at 1,443ppm TREO.

Axel recently secured environmental and water clearances for the start of the ISR program and is confirming municipal requirements for other authorisations such as approvals relating to permanent preservation areas or vegetation clearance.

It will test whether the leaching response demonstrated in earlier column work can be repeated consistently in the ground while also examining hydraulic response, operating parameters and the behaviour of the mineralised profile at larger scale.

Site-Specific Data

Managing director Dr Patience Mpofu said Axel expected the results of the WSP study to provide site-specific operating data to guide future wellfield design and the evaluation of potential larger-scale ISR operations.

“Following our recent success in producing high-grade mixed rare earth carbonate from laboratory-scale leach solutions, our next priority is to evaluate the performance of magnesium sulphate ISR under field conditions,” she said.

“This program will provide critical technical information to support our strategy to unlock the potential of the Woolrich rare earth deposit.”

In parallel with the WSP appointment, Axel has commenced a detailed auger drilling program within the designated 20,000-square-metre study area at Woolrich to improve the geological definition of the mineralised regolith and generate additional samples for magnesium sulphate leach testing.

The systematic data-driven approach will support the final design for the field program and provide a stronger technical foundation for evaluating the performance of magnesium sulphate ISR under representative site conditions.

data.title: Scentre's New Bear Feels Pessimistic on Store Closures — Market Talk
data.description: The impact of David Jones' financial problems on Australia's mall operators could be larger than most investors expect, UBS analysts warn. They observe that the closure of multiple David Jones department stores is widely seen as nothing but a modest near-term headwind for impacted REITs, which would then get a considerable medium-term opportunity to extract stronger rents from new occupants. "We hold a less optimistic view," the UBS team writes in a note. They see lost rents hitting for up to 36 months and see repurposing space as dilutive due to capital expenditure and cost of debt. UBS cuts mall operator Scentre's rating to sell from neutral, and lowers its target price on the stock by 12% to 3.45 Australian dollars. Shares are down 0.4% at A$3.555. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: CORPWATCH: India's IT giants turn captive tech centres into billion-dollar deals
data.description:
IntelliNews summary:

• TCS closed its takeover of Best Buy's Indian capability centre on October 15.

• Wipro paid $375mn for Olam's Mindsprint, and HCLTech is absorbing nearly 2,000 Guardian India staff.

• India hosted 2,117 GCCs employing about 2.36mn people in the 2026 fiscal year.

• Six cities hold about nine in ten GCC units, led by Bengaluru with more than 1,080.

____________________

India's largest IT services firm TCS is in early talks to absorb part of Bosch's Indian technology arm and up to 3,000 staff, Mint reported on November 18.

The German engineering and car-parts group is weighing the sale of some technology and product development work in India to cut costs, and its board is expected to take up the question in December. Bosch Group in India declined to comment, saying it does not respond to market speculation, Deccan Chronicle reported.

The work in play sits in Bosch Global Software Technologies, set up in Bengaluru in 1997 and now also present in Hyderabad, Pune and Coimbatore. India holds roughly four-fifths of Bosch's 28,900-strong global capability centre (GCC) workforce, about half of it in Bengaluru, according to Mint, so a 3,000-person carve-out would take about one in eight of the Indian headcount. Listed Bosch Ltd , the group's Indian car-parts arm, does not run the centres.

Multinationals built captive GCCs in India to do technology work in-house rather than pay an outsourcer, and the captives grew big enough to dent the outsourcers: HSBC analysts linked the Indian IT sector's weak growth in the 2024 and 2025 fiscal years partly to business lost to GCCs. The traffic now runs the other way, with vendors buying the captives and tying each purchase to a multi-year services contract. Bosch, which in June said it would shut its Sofia engineering centre with up to 670 jobs affected, is already trimming engineering costs elsewhere.

Staff moving to the buyer in captive technology centre takeovers by Indian IT services firms. The Bosch figure is from a press report of preliminary talks; the Best Buy headcount is a press estimate. Sources: Wipro, HCLTech, Infosys; Mint; Times of India. IntelliNews

The Best Buy template

TCS has run the same play once already this autumn. On October 1 it agreed with US electronics retailer Best Buy to take over the retailer's Indian GCC and rebuild it as an AI-focused hub, and an exchange filing shows the purchase of BBY Services India LLP closed on October 15. TCS beat Accenture and Wipro to a five-year mandate worth an estimated INR20bn ($216mn) covering a Bengaluru centre of about 600 people, the Times of India reported in September.

'By bringing that talent together with TCS' retail expertise, AI, engineering and global execution capabilities, we will create an AI-native capability engine that aligns Best Buy's priorities,' said Krishnan Ramanujam, president of TCS' consumer business group, in the announcement.

Bosch's engineers would land in a growing automotive book. In August TCS agreed to buy MHP, Porsche's consultancy, for an enterprise value of €320mn alongside a €1.25bn AI contract with the carmaker. The Bosch teams would give it depth in physical AI, the AI built into machines such as robots and self-driving cars, Mint reported, quoting Sushovon Nayak, lead IT analyst at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities, as saying long-term service contracts help IT firms lock in revenue for years.

Rivals in the same market

TCS' domestic rivals are working the same seam. Wipro completed its purchase of Mindsprint, the IT and digital arm of Singapore-based agribusiness Olam Group, with more than 3,200 staff, in May. It paid $375mn, and the deal came with an eight-year transformation contract that Wipro expects to be worth more than $1bn.

HCLTech said in July that it would take over Guardian India, the capability centre of US insurer Guardian Life, moving nearly 2,000 employees into a dedicated unit under a seven-year agreement; press reports of its filing put the price at $10.5mn. Infosys did the same in 2023 with Danske Bank's Indian IT centre and its 1,400-plus staff.

The vendors have no shortage of targets: India hosted 2,117 GCCs running 3,728 units and employing about 2.36mn people in the 2026 fiscal year, a Nasscom-Zinnov report found in July, with the number of centres up 32% since the 2021 fiscal year and revenue of $98.4bn. Software and IT-enabled services exports came to $221.4bn over the same year, and new entrants keep arriving: Costco picked Hyderabad for its first Indian technology centre in 2025.

GCC units by city in the 2026 fiscal year, with Bosch's Indian technology sites marked. Sources: Nasscom-Zinnov, GCC Value Orbit (July 2026); Mint; Natural Earth. IntelliNews

Six cities hold about nine in ten of those units, led by Bengaluru with more than 1,080, then Hyderabad, Delhi NCR, Pune, Chennai and Mumbai. Bosch follows the same map: three of its four Indian technology sites, in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune, are in the four biggest hubs, with only Coimbatore outside them.

The Mindsprint numbers show how the trade works for the seller. Olam took $375mn for its captive and signed up for a contract its buyer values at more than $1bn, turning a cost centre built to avoid outsourcing into the asset that sealed an outsourcing deal.

data.title: Hesai Group Announces Inclusion as a Constituent of the Hang Seng TECH Index
data.description:
SHANGHAI, China, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hesai Group (Nasdaq: HSAI; HKEX: 2525) (“Hesai” or the “Company”), a Physical AI infrastructure company, today announced that, according to the announcement published by Hang Seng Indexes Company Limited on November 20, 2026, the shares of the Company listed on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (stock code: 2525) will be included as a constituent stock of the Hang Seng TECH Index. The change will be implemented after the market close on Friday, December 4, 2026 and will take effect on Monday, December 7, 2026.

The Hang Seng TECH Index comprises only 50 Hong Kong-listed companies with high exposure to selected technology themes. The themes covered by the index are digital platforms and solutions, artificial intelligence, advanced hardware, robotics and automation, cloud, and frontier technologies.

The Company believes that inclusion in the Hang Seng TECH Index represents recognition by the capital market of the Company’s standing as a technology company, including its research and product capabilities, its business focus in Robotics and Physical AI, and the market capitalization and liquidity of its shares. The inclusion is expected to present the Company to a broader set of technology investors, broaden its investor base, and increase market attention to and trading liquidity in the shares.

The Company’s shares have been a constituent of the Hang Seng Composite Index since December 8, 2025.

The Company would like to thank shareholders and investors for their continued support. The Company will continue to develop its business and create long-term value for its shareholders.

About Hesai

Hesai Technology (Nasdaq: HSAI; HKEX: 2525) is a Physical AI infrastructure company. With a product portfolio spanning lidar, Kosmo spatial intelligence platform, and robotic actuation modules, Hesai is the only company in the industry covering the full robotics chain of “see, understand, and act” while achieving commercialization at scale. Leveraging full-stack proprietary ASIC capabilities and an integrated R&D-manufacturing approach, Hesai has established industry-leading positions across core physical AI domains, including autonomous mobility, spatial intelligence, embodied AI, and commercial robots, and holds a leading share of the global lidar market. Hesai has established offices in Shanghai, Palo Alto, and Stuttgart, and operates in-house factories in China and Thailand, with customers spanning more than 40 countries.

data.title: FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") Becomes Approved Robotics Supplier to Top-Tier U.S. Public School Districts, Forms Strategic Partnerships with School Districts, and Fulfills Their Robot Orders
data.description:
• FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") is now an approved robotics supplier to a top-tier California public school district and has joined its procurement platform which means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and its education productivity solutions directly.
  • The Company recently welcomed Carolyn Kissane as an independent director on FFR's board. As associate dean of NYU's Center for Global Affairs, she brings deep experience connecting academia, research, and industry. Her expertise will help expand FFR's robotics education ecosystem, strengthen partnerships, engage more developers, and accelerate its Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy across all four industry ecosystems.
  • Last week, FFR launched in Dubai, introducing six robots to the Middle East. With local partners, it showcased real-world applications across education, security, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports, marking a new chapter for Physical AI in the region.
  • FFAI reported its Q3 results last week and achieved a major milestone in financial governance. As of September 30, 2026, management concluded that all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting had been remediated and that related controls were operating effectively which will help build a stronger foundation for its businesses.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. () ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR.

"Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR's education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We've cleared the district's review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district's career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California's leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We'll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we'll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we're now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we've made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it's a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That's a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We'll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR's profile in the industry grows, we've received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I'll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week, we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR's board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University's Center for Global Affairs. data.title: Changzhou Microintelligence seeks up to $74.62 million in revived Hong Kong IPO
data.description:
China-based Changzhou Microintelligence (3275.HK) is looking to raise up to HK$584.9 million ($74.62 million) through its Hong Kong initial public offering to fund research and development, an exchange filing showed on Monday.

The industrial robot maker has set an indicative offer price range of HK$12.07 to HK$15.69 per share.

Here are some details:

  • The company withdrew its earlier Hong Kong IPO in October, which had sought to raise up to HK$799.9 million, citing prevailing market conditions

  • Changzhou Microintelligence shelved its initial listing plans amid a global technology selloff driven by concerns over the sustainability of the AI spending boom and whether returns would justify heavy investment across the sector

  • The new offering comprises 37.3 million H shares, of which about 33.5 million will be allocated to international investors

  • More than 60% of the proceeds will be used to develop the company's core technologies, with a focus on enhancing the intelligence and performance of its embodied intelligent industrial robot (EIIR) products

  • The company expects H shares to start trading on December 4

  • The new prospectus includes a downward price adjustment mechanism that would allow the offer price to be reduced to as low as HK$10.87 per share if market conditions warrant

($1 = 7.8389 Hong Kong dollars)

data.title: BHP unveils plans to double copper output in South Australia by 2040
data.description:
BHP , the world's top copper miner, revealed plans on Monday to double its South Australian copper production by 2040 at a cost of up to $18.1 billion, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

BHP said it had found a path to raise annual copper production from the operations to 650,000 metric tons, with investment of $14.2 billion to $18.1 billion. That would boost copper production from the region, which BHP says is the world's second-biggest for copper, and take it close to the capacity of the world's largest copper mine, Escondida in Chile.

The world's largest listed miner aims to produce 2 million tons of the metal, which is key to electrification, from its global operations by the middle of the next decade, and expects the Copper South Australia operations to deliver around one third of its copper growth to 2035.

When including expected byproducts such as uranium, gold and silver from Copper SA, BHP said that global production will be equivalent to 2.5 million tons of copper per year.

The Copper SA operations include Olympic Dam and the Carrapateena and Prominent Hill mines, which it acquired in 2023, and a 2018 discovery at Ankata, which was originally named Oak Dam.

BHP said it expects consolidation, the introduction of block caving, which is a type of bulk mining, and extended processing to significantly cut operating costs.

As part of the expansion, BHP will increase the capacity of its uranium processing plant to increase production by around half to 5,000 to 6,000 tons a year.

($1 = 1.5117 Australian dollars)

data.title: Development of BHP's Copper South Australia operations
data.description:
BHP , the world's top copper miner, unveiled plans on Monday to double its South Australian copper production by 2040 at a cost of up to $18.1 billion, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

The centrepiece of that plan, Olympic Dam, was intended to become a top-tier growth engine after BHP took over Western Mining Corporation in 2005. There have been multiple expansion concepts since then, but so far none of them has been executed.

1975 - Western Mining Corp discovers the Olympic Dam mineral deposit in the state of South Australia.

1979 - Joint venture formed with BP Group to develop the project.

1988 - Underground mining starts at an annual rate of 45,000 metric tons of copper, plus byproducts uranium oxide, gold and silver.

1995 - After a series of optimisation projects, Olympic Dam is producing 170,000 metric tons a year of copper and associated byproducts. It has conditional approval to increase that to 350,000 tons.

2005 - BHP acquires WMC, and with it Olympic Dam, for about A$9.2 billion.

2009 - BHP, under CEO Marius Kloppers, proposes a giant open-pit expansion and releases a draft environmental impact study, with plans to lift production by about 515,000 tons of copper per year above existing output.

2011 - The proposed expansion receives major approvals. Industry estimates at the time put the project cost at around $30 billion, which would have made it one of the world's largest mining developments.

2012 - BHP shelves the open-pit expansion. Kloppers says the project had become too costly, linking the decision to weaker commodity markets and the need for stricter capital allocation. The estimated capital bill remained around $30 billion.

2017 - BHP confirms it is investigating a brownfield expansion plan for Olympic Dam under CEO Andrew Mackenzie, which would raise production to 450,000 tons per year of copper from the mid-2020s.

2018 - BHP announces the discovery of the Oak Dam West copper-gold-uranium deposit about 65 km (40 miles) southeast of Olympic Dam, after drilling intersects one of the best copper discoveries in Australia in decades.

2019 - BHP's brownfield expansion plan is declared a major development by South Australia.

2020 - Mike Henry takes the helm of the world's biggest miner and BHP abandons the Olympic Dam expansion plan due to high costs. Instead, it focuses on a debottlenecking strategy which backs incremental investments in smelter, refinery and underground mine capacity rather than a multi-decade open-pit project.

2023 - BHP acquires Australian copper miner OZ Minerals for around A$9.6 billion and creates Copper South Australia by combining Olympic Dam with the former OZ Minerals assets, Prominent Hill and Carrapateena, which are in the same region.

2024-2026 - BHP focuses on lifting production across Copper South Australia through smelter expansion studies, mine growth and exploration, as well as integration of the three asset hubs.

2027 - BHP is due to make a final investment decision on the expansion project.

2063 - Planned closure of the operations.

data.title: Japan's wealthy bank accounts over JPY100mn jump 4.2%
data.description:
Japan had 154,200 personal bank accounts holding at least JPY100mn ($629,000) at the end of September, a 4.2% rise on the previous year, Jiji Press reported on November 21, citing a Bank of Japan survey.

Money in these large accounts is growing faster than household savings as a whole. Jiji Press attributed the trend to higher asset values driven by rising share prices, among other factors, and said wealth was becoming more concentrated among Japan's richest savers.

Combined balances in the accounts grew 5.0% year on year to JPY32.72 trillion. Total deposits held by individuals rose 1.3% over the same period.

The number of such accounts has increased 3.6-fold since the end of September 2000, the earliest point for which comparable figures exist.

Most of the large accounts fell into the lowest bracket covered by the survey. Some 135,800 held between JPY100mn and JPY300mn, while 15,600 contained from JPY300mn up to JPY1bn. Another 2,800 accounts had balances of JPY1bn or more.

Faraday Future CEO YT Jia Shares Weekly Update: FFAI’s Remediation of Nine Previously Identified Material Weaknesses in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting; FFR’s Multiple Strategic Education Partnerships and Robots Sales with Public Schools

“Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR’s education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We’ve cleared the district’s review and joined its procurement platform. This week, the district’s career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California’s leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We’ll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we’ll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we’re now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we’ve made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it’s a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That’s a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We’ll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR’s profile in the industry grows, we’ve received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I’ll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR’s board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University’s Center for Global Affairs. This progress puts us in a stronger position to meet our obligations as a public company, raise capital, and rebuild trust with investors. data.title: LTR Pharma Advances US Commercial Rollout of ROXUS Intranasal ED Treatment
data.description:
LTR Pharma has issued more than 500 bottles of rapid-onset intranasal erectile dysfunction (ED) treatment ROXUS since its US launch in October under the patient-specific 503A regulatory pathway.

Prescriptions have been fulfilled across 43 US states through direct-to-consumer telehealth company Shed Holdings (under a distribution agreement signed in July) and Strive Compounding Pharmacy.

Shed is leading digital patient acquisition through an initial phase that includes assessing patient experience, retention, and repeat activity to inform broader scaling of marketing activity.

As ROXUS is an on-demand treatment, patient usage and re-order timing will vary and LTR believes repeat purchasing and retention trends will become clearer as the initial cohorts mature.

LTR has invoiced Strive and received its first US revenue and prescribing, fulfilment, invoicing and payment infrastructure now operational.

Advancing Customer Reach

Alongside Shed, LTR is developing a separate healthcare professional and direct-to-clinic channel that will allow clinics to prescribe ROXUS for eligible patients while Strive Pharmacy fulfils the prescriptions.

Work to enable ROXUS within established electronic prescribing workflows has progressed, including connectivity through electronic prescribing network Surescripts, which is used by 1.39 million prescribers and 98.3% of US pharmacies.

Initial prescribing has commenced through a small number of clinics including Prime Institute in Florida and Urology Partners in North Texas.

These clinics are operated by LTR scientific advisory board members Dr Amy Pearlman and Dr Andrew Sun, respectively.

LTR is also continuing clinician education following its attendance at the Sexual Medicine Society of North America annual scientific meeting in October, where it engaged with US specialists regarding intranasal PDE5 therapy, administration and Australian real-world experience.

Valuable Market Insights

LTR executive chair Lee Rodne said the fulfillment milestone demonstrated the geographical reach and licensure of the company’s partner network.

“Reaching more than 500 bottles is an encouraging early milestone and the initial US rollout gives us valuable insights into demand, treatment response, and the patient experience,” he said.

“It has reinforced the importance of first-use education and administration guidance, consistent with our experience in Australia, and we are working closely with Shed and Strive to apply these learnings to patient education, onboarding, and provider support before progressively scaling commercial activity.”

“Our focus at this stage is establishing the patient experience, retention and prescribing pathways required to support sustainable broader adoption.”

Indian Patent Granted

The Indian Patent Office has granted LTR with a patent to protect defined formulation characteristics of the intranasal technology supporting lead products SPONTAN and ROXUS through to May 2041.

The fast-acting intranasal sprays enable onset of action in 10 minutes or less, compared with 60 minutes for the 20 milligram oral vardenafil tablet.

“The grant of this patent in India is a positive milestone for LTR Pharma, further strengthening the intellectual property portfolio supporting SPONTAN and ROXUS,” Mr Rodne said.

“Protecting our intellectual property remains an important part of our strategy as we advance our clinical and commercial programs.”
